name: Banner
summary: Prominent message spanning a wide region.

a11y.apg: Same live-region rule as Alert: `danger` is role="alert", the rest role="status". The only focusable thing is the dismiss button, and it appears only when you pass `onDismiss` — reachable by Tab, with an accessible name from the i18n strings.

props.name: variant
props.description: Tone, and the same live-region rule as Alert: `danger` is role="alert", the rest role="status".

props.name: title
props.description: Rendered as a <strong> above the body.

props.name: icon
props.description: Carbon glyph in the leading column. Leave it out and the column still holds its place — an empty span keeps the three-column grid — so banners stacked together stay aligned.

props.name: onDismiss
props.description: Passing it is what draws the close button. Without it the banner cannot be dismissed, which is the right default for something the reader has to see.

props.name: state
props.type: waiting_user | waiting_approval | waiting_dependency | offline | stale | partial | degraded
props.description: Universal state (Part J) — same axis and same derivation as on Alert: `variant` is severity, `state` is the condition. It sets `data-state`, picks the severity when no `variant` is given, and supplies the message when there are no children. A banner is the page-width place to say “no connection” or “working with reduced capability”, which is why it carries the same vocabulary as the inline alert instead of a second one.
